description: brig·id: the one Renovate preset, extended by every repository with
{ "extends": ["github>brig-id/.github"] }.
Renovate opens pull requests and never merges them. A repository gets at most, on a
Monday, one pull request for everything from outside the project and one for the
project's own releases; a lock file refresh a month; a security fix at once. A major
version waits on the Dependency Dashboard until its box is ticked.

schedule: before 7am on the first day of the month

description: A tag and its commit, written together and annotated on the line above:
# renovate: datasource=github-tags depName=brig-id/app
The key may also be a variable whose name ends in REF: APP_REF: <40 hex> # v1.2.3.
Both are updated in one pull request: the commit is what is built, the tag says which release it is.
An update from outside the project is not a release of its own: build(deps), which
release-please leaves out; it ships with the next release. config:recommended would make
a runtime dependency fix(deps), and each one would open a release pull request. A security
fix is the exception (vulnerabilityAlerts above).

packageRules.description: Everything from outside the project but a major: ONE pull request a week per repository.
A major version is a decision: one pull request each, opened from the Dependency Dashboard.

description: The project's own releases (crypto, core, app): all in ONE pull request per repository,
on the same Monday schedule; its box on the Dependency Dashboard opens it at once when it
is wanted sooner. The core, crypto and the interface move together, and two versions of
the core in one build do not compile. It comes in as build(deps), whatever the kind of
update: it releases nothing, and the dependent ships it with its next release (a fix or
a feature of its own), or when its owner asks for one. Otherwise one change of the core
would release the core, then every server and the interface in turn. Not brig-id/.github: its reusable workflows are
pinned by a commit without a tag, which Renovate does not follow; they are moved by hand.
A server is never part of what is released elsewhere: the interface and the demo only test
against it. Its update is ci, which releases nothing; otherwise each release of the interface
would release a server, which would release the interface again, without end.
